title: Ukraine's Ground Robots Rescued 45 Soldiers Under Fire, Commander Says
key_facts: Ground robots of the Artan special unit, part of Ukraine's Military Intelligence Directorate (HUR), evacuated 45 soldiers from under Russian fire during summer 2026, per the unit.
The platforms covered a combined 4,258 kilometers (2,646 miles) and delivered more than 41 tons of supplies to frontline positions.
Tasks also included evacuating wounded troops and transporting captured Russian soldiers.
Artan commander Col. Viktor Torkotiuk, call sign Titan, spoke to RBC-Ukraine.
The unit did not say how many vehicles took part, how many trips were made or which robot models were used.
Artan mainly operates on the Zaporizhzhia front in southern Ukraine and took part in one stage of Operation Vivaldi near Lyman.
Kyiv Post says President Volodymyr Zelensky set a target of at least 50,000 ground robotic systems for the military in 2026.
Soldiers have told Kyiv Post that robots are not replacing troops but take on the most dangerous supply and medical evacuation runs.
quote_evidence: Ukraine's ground robots rescued 45 soldiers from under Russian fire and transported more than 41 tons of supplies to frontline positions during the summer of 2026, according to the Artan special unit under Ukraine's Military Intelligence Directorate (HUR).
The unit did not specify how many vehicles took part in the missions, how many individual journeys they completed, or which ground-robot models they used.
"Technology is transforming the combat capabilities of units on the front line," Torkotiuk said.
why_it_matters_hint: Robots take over the most exposed evacuation and supply runs where ordinary vehicles are quickly spotted by drones.
event_date: Summer 2026 (figures announced by the unit, reported 9 Oct 2026)
notes: All figures are the unit's own, relayed by RBC-Ukraine and Kyiv Post; no independent check and no vehicle or trip counts. Figures cover the summer campaign, announced 9 Oct 2026, so treated as NEW. Pool score 7 set by Rafi's order of 10 Oct 2026 (curator score 5).
